project_tracker_diagnostic: Low multi-trunked shrub/small tree on dry limestone; flaky/papery bark; variable shallowly lobed leaves; very shallow saucer-like acorn cup enclosing about one-quarter of the nut or less.
verified_target_counties: Hays; Travis; Blanco; Burnet; Comal; Gillespie; Kerr; Bandera; Edwards; Real; Uvalde; Crockett; Kimble

morphology_keys.habit: Shrub or small tree usually to about 3–5 m, often forming thickets with multiple trunks near ground level.
morphology_keys.bark: Gray to light brown, flaky to papery and exfoliating.
morphology_keys.leaves: Highly variable, from nearly entire to irregularly toothed or sinuately lobed; underside often has minute appressed stellate hairs.
morphology_keys.acorn: Cup saucer-shaped to shallowly cup-shaped, generally enclosing only about 1/8–1/4 of the nut.

photo_strategy.oak_specific_tightening: Prioritize multi-photo late-summer/fall observations to increase the chance of mature leaves and acorns, plus curated taxon reference photos.
